difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 9.4.14 at source lines 812-814: for categories A and B a functor is an equivalence of categories if and only if it is an isomorphism of categories. The author's proof (source lines 815-825) is short because both properties are mere propositions, but each direction consumes a different retained result: the forward direction turns the natural isomorphisms into identities of the composites with the retained functor-category theorem and then reads off that the object map is an equivalence (lines 817-820), while the converse builds split essential surjectivity from the inverse object map (lines 822-823) and invokes the retained characterisation of equivalences of precategories to finish (line 824). The statement is a two-way implication between named notions and records neither of the two inputs nor the reduction of the properties to propositions.
